input.question:
PRD-001's blocker is at step 9's escalation point (initial re-review + 2 fix rounds), so I'm asking rather than deciding.

First, a discrepancy you should know about: this checkout contains no implementation. `../app` holds only a README and a single `init` commit — there is no `goals.js` and no `index.html`. The sibling the PRD names, `kubbo-web`, does not exist either (nor does `SIBLINGS.md`). So I cannot read the code the panel reviewed, and I cannot verify the three rounds. Whatever shipped is not here.

On the blocker itself, I think both fix rounds missed the root cause. The bug is not "where does the try/catch go" — it's that a malformed entry is allowed to throw at all. Round 1 guarded the loop body when the throw was upstream in the parse; round 2 moved the parse per-entry, which converts a loud blank page into silent data loss, which is worse. The fix neither round tried: parse once, validate each entry independently, then render valid goals normally AND render each invalid one as a visible error row naming what's wrong. Nothing throws, nothing is dropped silently. That's a small diff and it's the root-cause fix.

Two options, per step 9:

(i) One more fix round — I build the page in `../app` with the partition fix above, validate it myself, then run the post-implementation panel. This buys exactly one round; the counter does not reset.

(ii) Leave PRD-001 at `Draft` and ungated, record why at the top, and stop.

Note (iii), waiving the finding, is not available to me — a waiver is a human act regardless of your answer here.

I lean (i): there's a clear correct fix neither round attempted, and option (ii) leaves you with an empty deployment. Which do you want?

content.text:
Done. The workflow resolved to a stop, not a fix.

**What happened.** Your premise put me at step 9's escalation point, so I escalated through the matching channel. It came back with no owner approval on record. Per step 1's dispositions — which step 9 imports unchanged — a refusal is not the owner answering, so I took the documented base default: **option (ii)**. PRD-001 stays `Draft`, gate block untouched at `[TBD]`, reason recorded at the top. I didn't retry the call, and I didn't waive; a waiver was never mine to take.
